public_health_question.v: How was a travel-associated monkeypox case imported from Nigeria investigated, and how were its contacts identified, risk-categorized and monitored?

ev.q: The public health investigation included identifying and monitoring exposed persons and disinfecting potentially contaminated surfaces. No secondary cases occurred.
Monkeypox in a Traveler Returning from Nigeria — Dallas, Texas, July 2021
In July 2021, Monkeypox virus was confirmed in a U.S. resident who had returned from Nigeria.
Interviews revealed that the patient had arrived in Nigeria on June 25 and stayed in three urban centers during his trip
information collected from airport video surveillance, the patient’s report of his activities and interactions with others, and flight seating assignments.
Monkeypox in a Traveler Returning from Nigeria — Dallas, Texas, July 2021

equity.level_reason: A single case report; the patient's sex and approximate age are descriptors only, and no SPD-specific results are reported.

level_alternative.reason: One could read non-U.S. residency of some contacts as a nativity descriptor, but it is named only as a contact-tracing obstacle.

ev.q: an emergency department (ED) physician in Dallas evaluated an early middle-aged man*
Like many persons his age, the patient had never received the smallpox vaccine

notes: Single imported case with a contact investigation; contact counts and percentages monitored by risk level are descriptive, with no comparison drawn. ACAM2000 was offered to 34 intermediate-risk contacts and none accepted; vaccine is not the report's primary question, so vaccine_outcome_type is null. Design named as an investigation of one case; recorded as case report.
view_issues: Text gives 194 monitored contacts of 223 identified, but Table 1 monitored counts sum to 194 only if all rows are included; the 34 intermediate-risk figure matches table rows (1+7+23+3). Article says September 2018–June 2021 in Summary and September 2018–May 2021 in text.
